targeting.title: n8n Schedule Trigger: Fix Timezone, Cron and Not Running Issues
targeting.metaTitle: n8n Schedule Trigger: Timezone and Cron Fixes
targeting.metaDescription: Fix an n8n Schedule Trigger that is not running or fires at the wrong time. Covers publishing, timezone, cron syntax and durable scheduler timing.
targeting.excerpt: A source-checked n8n Schedule Trigger guide, verified against the n8n 2.47.7 release: why a schedule does not run until you publish, which timezone it reads, how each interval is timed on the durable scheduler, tested cron examples and what happens to missed runs.
targeting.keywords: n8n schedule trigger, n8n schedule trigger not working, n8n schedule trigger time zone, n8n schedule trigger change timezone, n8n schedule trigger cron, n8n schedule trigger not running, n8n schedule trigger weekdays, n8n cron expression, n8n invalid cron expression, n8n generic_timezone, n8n set timezone docker, n8n schedule trigger multiple times, n8n schedule trigger random
targeting.summary: A Schedule Trigger only fires after the workflow is published, and it reads times in the workflow timezone or else the instance timezone|From n8n 2.45.0 seconds and minutes intervals count from publication, while hours, days, weeks, months and cron rules follow the clock|Use plain five-field cron syntax, remember that day of month and day of week combine as OR, and choose a missed-run option if restarts matter
targeting.author: Ali Rehman

overlap.finding: Thirteen published n8n posts. The Schedule Trigger is mentioned twice in the beginner guide and once in the date format guide, with no heading about schedules, cron or timezone settings in any post. No dedicated Schedule Trigger, cron or instance timezone guide exists on the site.

research.selection: Ran 44 n8n seeds through Google public autocomplete on 16 November 2026. The Schedule Trigger seed returned ten suggestions, six of them troubleshooting or timezone wording (time zone, not working, change timezone, not running, doesn't work, random), and the related timezone seeds (n8n timezone, n8n set timezone, n8n generic_timezone) returned more than twenty further variants. Error handling (error workflow not triggering, retry on fail, continue on fail) was the runner-up cluster and stays open for the next post. Search results for these queries already include the official docs, community threads and many blog guides, so this is not a low-competition claim. The differentiator is coverage of the durable scheduler that became the default in n8n 2.45.0, backed by running n8n's own scheduling code.

primarySourceNotes: ScheduleTrigger.node.ts at n8n@2.47.7: versions 1 to 1.4; seven Trigger Interval options; manual mode uses rules[0], skips the recurrence check and validates a cron rule with sendAt from the cron package; registration failures of a cron rule are rethrown as 'Invalid cron expression'; misfire options shown from node version 1.4; default weekday [0] (Sunday).

GenericFunctions.ts: toCronExpression fills the second (and a missing minute, hour or day of month) from a sha256 of workflowId:nodeId; seconds rules are */N with no offset; minutes not dividing 60 and hours not dividing 24 fire every period and are gated; validateInterval messages and ranges.

schedule-trigger-job-registrar.ts: durable interception when N8N_SCHEDULER_ENABLED and N8N_USE_WORKFLOW_PUBLICATION_SERVICE are on (both default true); seconds and minutes become interval jobs in the default 'new' mode; every N hours, days, weeks, months with N >= 2 become recurring_cron; everything else plain cron; workflow timezone '' or 'DEFAULT' resolves to the instance timezone; first run computed with computeFirstRunAt.

@n8n/scheduler recurrence code: interval adds elapsed seconds; cron uses cron-parser with Luxon zones (missing local time shifts forward, repeated time fires once); recurring_cron fires a candidate in the same period as the previous fire or at least N periods later; weeks start on Sunday.
schedule-trigger-task-handler.ts builds the trigger item from task.scheduledFor, so the durable item's timestamp is the scheduled time.
Config defaults at the tag: GENERIC_TIMEZONE America/New_York, scheduler enabled true, triggerNodeMode 'new', DEFAULT_MISFIRE_GRACE_SECONDS 60.
pnpm catalog at the tag pins cron 4.4.0, cron-parser 5.6.1, luxon 3.7.2, moment-timezone 0.5.48.

n8n docs: publish requirement, timezone order and defaults, durable scheduler default from 2.45.0, misfire options from 2.36 on newly added nodes, variables evaluated at publication, Cloud console timezone steps, Docker GENERIC_TIMEZONE and TZ.
Editor text at the tag: Publish, Unpublish, Timezone, 'Default - {defaultTimezoneValue}'.
